query: How do review themes differ between positive and negative IMDb sentiment?

per_column.name: sentiment_description
per_column.rationale: Its two values (positive/negative) are a direct textual restatement of the focus variable label_pos; segmenting on it just reproduces the focus, offering no external relationship.

per_column.name: review_character_count
per_column.rationale: Length is an external associational variable comparable against sentiment, but the distribution is degenerate: 184 of ~250 values are capped at 700, so it is near-constant and cannot support meaningful segmentation as observed.

per_column.name: detected_themes
per_column.rationale: Interpretable, well-separated thematic categories (plot, acting, directing, etc.) that can be grouped and compared against positive vs negative sentiment; directly serves the query about theme differences.

per_column.name: positive_sentiment_words
per_column.rationale: A small-integer count with interpretable, comparable buckets (0-4) that can be segmented against sentiment; associational rather than a restatement, though somewhat close to the sentiment construct.

per_column.name: negative_sentiment_words
per_column.rationale: Interpretable low-cardinality count that can be grouped and compared against the focus; provides an informative lexical signal correlated with sentiment.

per_column.name: sentiment_word_ratio
per_column.rationale: A derived ratio of the two word counts; it is an opaque score whose values are fragmented across many fine-grained fractions and largely restates the pos/neg word columns, weakening interpretable segmentation.

judge.rationale: The set contains one strong, directly-on-topic EDA variable (detected_themes) with clean interpretable categories, plus usable lexical counts (positive/negative sentiment words) that can be segmented against sentiment. However, several columns dilute the set: sentiment_description merely restates label_pos, review_character_count is near-constant (capped at 700) and thus non-informative as observed, and sentiment_word_ratio is a fragmented derived score that largely duplicates the word-count columns. As a whole it supports discovering some interpretable relationships with the focus but is weakened by restatement and degenerate/opaque columns.
